## Why This Is Asked
Shows mastery of low-level bit tricks and edge-case handling in constrained environments.

## Key Concepts
- Next permutation with fixed popcount using bit hacks
- Branchless arithmetic for speed
- Fixed-width overflow behavior

## Code Example
```javascript
uint64_t nextHigherWithSamePopcount(uint64_t n) {
  uint64_t c = n & -n;
  uint64_t r = n + c;
  return (((n ^ r) >> 2) / c) | r;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for arbitrary width (128-bit)?
- How does this interact with compiler optimizations and undefined behavior in signed contexts?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to derive a fast, branch-conscious solution for 128-bit integers; assesses comprehension of leading-zero concept and how to extend 64-bit intrinsics to 128 bits.

## Key Concepts

- Leading zeros counting in wide integers
- 64-bit intrinsics (clz) or portable fallbacks
- Branchless or minimal-branch reasoning for performance

## Code Example

```c
int countLeadingZeros128(uint128 x){
  if (x.hi != 0) return __builtin_clzll(x.hi);
  return 64 + __builtin_clzll(x.lo);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you implement portable clz without compiler intrinsics?
- How would you extend to 256-bit widths with identical patterns?

This technique is essential in:
- Cryptography (byte-swap operations for AES, SHA)
- Network protocol implementations ( endianness conversion)
- Low-level systems programming where timing-constant operations matter
